# Two changes from the v1 table
column2: both required by the layered design:

column1: #  1. An 8 KiB "nvdata" partition of custom subtype 0x40
column2: which Fls owns outright. Fee builds crash-safe

column1: #     EEPROM emulation on it and NvM builds CRC-protected
column2: redundant blocks on that. It MUST NOT be shared

column1: #     with nvs or spiffs: both relocate and rewrite entries as they see fit
#     that a written record stays where it was put. Two 4 KiB sectors is the minimum that lets Fee
#     ping-pong
column2: so that a garbage collection never has a moment with no valid copy of a block.

column1: #  2. spiffs shrinks from 0x30000 to 0x2E000 -- by exactly the 8 KiB nvdata takes -- and still runs to the
#     end of the device. Nothing in v2 uses SPIFFS -- all bulk data goes to the SD card -- but the partition
#     is kept
column2: because the OTA rollback path can land on a v1 image
column3: and a v1 image that cannot mount SPIFFS

column1: #     fails in a way nobody would connect to a partition table change made two releases earlier.
# The two app slots are unchanged and each hold 1.875 MiB
column2: which is what makes A/B OTA possible: a failed

column1: # update leaves the previous image bootable in the other slot.
# Offsets must stay sector-aligned (4 KiB) and the table must not exceed the 4 MiB device. Fls_Init verifies
# at runtime that the flashed table actually contains nvdata at the expected size
# separate artefact from the firmware and the two can disagree.
